issues.legal_issue: A statutory provision assigning a forum to decide who is the lawful ryot of a holding after an estate is notified is not confined to disputes about arrears of rent.
material_facts: The disputed lands were in an estate that had been taken over by the government under an abolition and ryotwari-settlement scheme.
The parties made rival claims to be the lawful ryots of the holding.
The governing scheme provided for ryotwari pattas for ryots but, under the narrower interpretation advanced, contained no other mechanism for deciding competing claims by ryots.
issues.conclusion: The provision covers disputes over who is the lawful ryot of a holding generally, and is not limited to identifying a person liable for rent arrears that accrued before the estate was taken over.
issues.legal_principle: Statutory interpretation, contextual or otherwise, must further rather than frustrate the statute’s object. Read in light of the scheme’s purpose of conferring ryotwari pattas on ryots and abolishing intermediaries, the provision for determining who is the lawful ryot cannot be restricted to the purposes of the rent-arrears provisions. The Court approved the five-Judge Full Bench decision in I. Munuswami Naidu v. R. Venkata Reddy and rejected Cherukuru Muthayya v. Gadde Gopalakrishnayya to the extent it imposed that restriction; the relevant provisions include Sections 55 and 56(1)(a)–(c), read with Sections 3, 11 and 15 of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Area) Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948.

predicates.notified_estate: The government had formally notified and taken over an estate under a scheme for abolishing intermediaries and introducing ryotwari settlement.
predicates.lawful_ryot_dispute: Two or more claimants disputed who was the lawful ryot of a holding in the estate.
predicates.ryot_pattta_framework_exists: The governing scheme provided for ryots to obtain ryotwari pattas in respect of qualifying lands.

issues.definition: When an estate has been notified, a dispute over who is its lawful ryot can be decided beyond the limited purpose of identifying liability for rent arrears if the governing scheme provides for ryots to obtain ryotwari pattas.

issues.legal_issue: A special statutory forum has exclusive jurisdiction over a dispute assigned to it concerning who is the lawful ryot of a holding after an estate is notified, even when that dispute arises in an eviction proceeding.
material_facts: The appellant sought eviction of the respondents for alleged non-payment of rent, claiming to be their landlord.
The respondents claimed that they and their ancestors had occupancy rights and were the lawful ryots of the land, which was in an estate taken over by the government.
The eviction proceedings therefore raised a dispute over who was the lawful ryot of the holding.
The statute assigned disputes about lawful ryot status after notification to a Settlement Officer, provided an appeal to a special tribunal, and made the tribunal’s decision final.
issues.conclusion: The Settlement Officer and the special tribunal had exclusive jurisdiction to decide the dispute over lawful ryot status; the eviction proceeding could not determine that issue, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Act is a self-contained code providing specially constituted tribunals to adjudicate specified disputes arising after notification of an estate. On general principles, those tribunals have exclusive jurisdiction over disputes entrusted to them by the statute. The Court relied on Appanna v. Sriramamurthy and approved I. Munuswami Naidu v. R. Venkata Reddy; Sections 56(1)(c) and 56(2) assign the lawful-ryot dispute to the Settlement Officer and provide for an appeal to the Estates Abolition Tribunal, whose decision is final.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding and notified_estate and lawful_ryot_dispute and special_forum_assigned_dispute

predicates.eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking to evict an occupant from land on an asserted landlord-tenant relationship.
predicates.notified_estate: The government had formally notified and taken over the estate containing the land.
predicates.lawful_ryot_dispute: The parties disputed who was the lawful ryot of the holding.
predicates.special_forum_assigned_dispute: The governing scheme assigned disputes of this kind to a specially constituted forum and provided for review by a special tribunal.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding concerns land in a notified estate and raises a dispute over who is the lawful ryot, the specially designated forum decides that dispute if the governing scheme assigns it there.
